display.purpose: The largest headline on a page: hero, section H1-scale moments. Always uppercase.

headline.purpose: Standard section headline (.h2), following every section's eyebrow + hairline.

body.purpose: Running body copy and sub-line intros under headlines.

label.purpose: Indices, meta lines, nav links, footer legal text, stage tags — anything numeric or meta is set in mono to read as data.

shadows.name: active-glow
shadows.purpose: The Process rail's active-stage dot only. The single permitted glow in an otherwise flat system — marks current state, never decorative.

motion.name: ease-precise
motion.purpose: The system's one easing curve, used for every hover/reveal/scroll transition.

motion.name: dur-med
motion.purpose: Hover/reveal transitions (hairline extend, description reveal, button color change).

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions (link color change, magnetic button snap-back).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one CTA style. Hard corners, Vintage Yellow fill, uppercase mono-tracked label.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.76rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 17px 30px; border: none; border-radius: 0; background: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); color: var(--kynetik-black, #202020); transition: background 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background: #f2cd7d; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action style (e.g. View / Download links).
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.76rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 17px 30px; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--foster-white, #ECECEC); border: 1px solid rgba(236,236,236,0.35); transition: border-color 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), color 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover, .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { border-color: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); color: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Primary navigation link, uppercase mono-tracked, low-opacity at rest.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; opacity: 0.85; color: var(--foster-white, #ECECEC); text-decoration: none; padding-bottom: 4px; position: relative; transition: opacity 220ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { opacity: 1; color: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); }

components.name: Numbered Tile
components.description: The system's signature repeating content unit (Offerings, What We Make): mono index, uppercase title, hairline rule that extends on hover, description revealed on hover (unconditionally visible on touch).
components.html:
01

3D Scanning & Modeling

We scan and model every surface in three dimensions, the exact foundation a perfect carbon fit demands.
components.css: .ds-tile { position: relative; background: var(--kynetik-black, #202020); border-top: 1px solid var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); padding: 32px 30px; min-height: 230px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; cursor: pointer; transition: background 900ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-tile:hover, .ds-tile:focus-visible { background: rgba(233,190,95,0.05); } .ds-tile-index { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); color: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; margin: 0 0 auto; } .ds-tile-title { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif); font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1.25; margin: 24px 0 10px; } .ds-tile-rule { width: 28px; height: 1px; background: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); border: 0; margin: 0 0 12px; transition: width 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-rule, .ds-tile:focus-visible .ds-tile-rule { width: 56px; } .ds-tile-desc { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size: 0.78rem; line-height: 1.55; color: rgba(236,236,236,0.55); max-height: 0; opacity: 0; overflow: hidden; margin: 0; transition: max-height 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), opacity 220ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-desc, .ds-tile:focus-visible .ds-tile-desc { max-height: 90px; opacity: 1; }

components.name: Value Column
components.description: Full-width statement column (What We Stand For): a large de-emphasised number, title, hairline, hover-revealed description. A tall variant of the Numbered Tile pattern for a five-across statement layout rather than a grid of cards.
components.html:
01

Design Fidelity

Every line stays true to the sketch that started it. Nothing is value-engineered away.
components.css: .ds-value { position: relative; border-left: 1px solid rgba(236,236,236,0.22); padding: 0 28px; min-height: 300px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: flex-end; cursor: pointer; transition: background 900ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-value:hover, .ds-value:focus-visible { background: rgba(236,236,236,0.03); } .ds-value-num { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size: clamp(2.2rem,4vw,3.4rem); line-height: 1; color: rgba(236,236,236,0.22); margin: 0; transition: color 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-value:hover .ds-value-num, .ds-value:focus-visible .ds-value-num { color: rgba(236,236,236,0.4); } .ds-value-title { margin: 20px 0 0; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif); font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-size: 1.1rem; color: var(--foster-white, #ECECEC); } .ds-value-rule { width: 28px; height: 1px; background: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); border: 0; margin: 16px 0 12px; transition: width 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-value:hover .ds-value-rule, .ds-value:focus-visible .ds-value-rule { width: 56px; } .ds-value-desc { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size: 0.78rem; line-height: 1.55; color: rgba(236,236,236,0.55); max-width: 26ch; max-height: 0; opacity: 0; overflow: hidden; margin: 0; transition: max-height 500ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), opacity 220ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-value:hover .ds-value-desc, .ds-value:focus-visible .ds-value-desc { max-height: 100px; opacity: 1; }

components.name: Hairline
components.description: The system's single recurring signature gesture: a 1px rule that draws in from width 0 to 56px as its section scrolls into view, and extends further on hover at component scale. Reuse this for any new divider, underline, or active-state indicator instead of inventing a new one.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif); font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.24em; font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); margin: 0; } .ds-hairline { width: 0; height: 1px; background: var(--vintage-yellow, #E9BE5F); border: 0; margin: 22px 0 0; transition: width 1.1s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-hairline.is-in { width: 56px; }

narrative.overview: Kynetik Koncepts reads like a workshop drawing, not a SaaS marketing site: numbered indices, monospace labels, hairline rules, and full-bleed real photography stand in for the decoration a typical luxury-brand microsite would reach for. The system is restrained, precise, and technical — every element earns its place through repetition and discipline (01 through 09, always), not through embellishment. Vintage Yellow is spent like a signature stamp, not a paint color: it marks the thing that matters on a given screen (an eyebrow, a hairline, the one CTA) and stays absent everywhere else. Depth and warmth come from the real photography and deep, near-black grounds, not from surface treatment. Type stays quiet and functional so the car photography and the workshop-drawing motifs (indices, rails, hairlines) carry the emotional weight instead.
keyCharacteristics: Flat-by-default: no card shadows anywhere; the one exception (a soft glow on the Process rail's active-stage dot) is a deliberate, rare signal, never decoration.
Sharp corners everywhere except true circles (cursor ring/dot, the rail's progress dot, the reduced-motion process icon badge) — no soft-rounded cards.
Every tile, panel, and value column carries a two-digit mono index (01, 02, 03...) like a catalogue or blueprint sheet entry.
Resting state is deliberately plain; craft shows up in the hover/reveal transition (hairline extends, description reveals), not the default state.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Vintage Yellow appears on a small fraction of any given screen — an eyebrow, a hairline, one button, a handful of index numbers. If a new element reaches for a second saturated color, that's the signal something has gone off-brand.

rules.name: The Gold-on-Olive Rule
rules.body: The Vintage Yellow accent must never sit directly on Olive Green — a strict brand-guideline rule preserved even though Olive Green isn't in current use.

rules.name: The Uppercase-and-Tracked Rule
rules.body: Anything set in Space Grotesk is uppercase with deliberate letter-spacing; the font never appears in sentence case. Reserve sentence-case, tighter-tracked type for Helvetica body copy only.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay flat at rest. The only depth cue permitted is the Vintage Yellow glow, and only to mark active/current state on a progress indicator — never applied to cards, buttons, or panels for decoration.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every section headline is followed by a 1px Vintage Yellow rule that animates from width:0 to 56px as the section scrolls into view, and the same motif reappears at tile/component scale, extending from 28px to 56px on hover. Any new section or component that needs a divider, underline, or active-state indicator should reuse this pattern rather than inventing a new one.

dos: Do reserve Vintage Yellow for one signal per screen — an eyebrow, a hairline, one button, index numbers. Never a second saturated color alongside it.
Do reuse the hairline-draw / hairline-extend motif for new dividers, underlines, or active-state indicators (see The Hairline Rule).
Do keep new "labeled item" grids (cards, tiles, columns) in the Numbered Tile pattern: mono index, uppercase title, hairline rule, hover/touch-revealed description.
Do make any newly revealed content (a hover description, an expanded detail) unconditionally visible under max-width:900px so touch devices aren't locked out of it.
Do match real photography to a section by what it actually depicts; flag a gap rather than force a mismatch (see PRODUCT.md's Product Principles).
donts: Don't add card shadows, glassmorphism, or gradient fills. The system is flat by default; the only permitted glow is the Vintage Yellow active-state signal on the Process rail.
Don't introduce an intermediate border-radius. Corners are either hard 0px or true 50% circles.

Don't reopen the Carbon Grey ground on the Impact section as a "make it more colorful" problem — it's a confirmed brand choice; layout, spacing, and interaction are the tools for fixing a flat-feeling section, not color.
Don't place the Vintage Yellow accent directly on Olive Green, even though Olive Green is currently unused (The Gold-on-Olive Rule).
Don't set Space Grotesk in sentence case, or drop its uppercase/tracked treatment — that contrast against Helvetica body copy is what gives the hierarchy its structure.
